category: premium file host (one-click hoster), retrieval target

free_tier.stated: Free tier is not quantified by the vendor on the premium page: it advertises only that 'Premium members can skip the public countdown, use direct downloads, and get larger transfer allowances.'

retention.stated: premium files are deleted when the premium plan lapses, per a reseller's reading of the terms; not confirmed on the vendor page

egress.terms: Premium is sold as no speed limit and no download limit, with a separate 'TrafficShare' allowance quoted at 1 TB per month by a third party. Free downloads carry a public countdown and ads.
egress.free_allowance: 1 TB/month TrafficShare reported; the premium download path itself is advertised as unlimited

interface_detail: No API documentation reachable; the site is a client-rendered application and returned the home page for /premium.
tooling: browser; download managers supported per the premium feature list
chaining: Only useful if a user's links are FileFactory links; its 2025-era share of link-site posts is small next to Rapidgator and 1fichier.

limits.value: free downloads run behind a public countdown and ads; no rate published
free downloads are shaped; premium claims unlimited bandwidth with no number

limits_note: 'Unlimited bandwidth' is a marketing claim with no fair-use number attached that was reachable.
binding_note: Nothing in the reachable pages caps volume, so the only thing that can fail at 1 TiB/month is throughput or an unpublished fair-use throttle.

identity_cost.detail: Account creation is e-mail. Payment is by card; a reseller also sells keys.

reliability_note: The vendor states premium accounts revert to free on expiry and that files and folders are permanently deleted if the plan is not renewed.
confidence_note: Every number here is from a third party because /premium is client-rendered and served the home page. The vendor's own pricing page is the route that would raise this to documented.

evidence.proved: returned the site shell: 'Premium members can skip the public countdown, use direct downloads, and get larger transfer allowances'
reseller table: 30 days $13, 90 $35, 180 $59, 365 $94; TrafficShare 100 GB/month on one page and 1 TB elsewhere
Premium is sold on 'unlimited bandwidth'; the page renders its price grid client-side and returned no price to the reader.

price_per_tb_month: USD 13.00 per TiB-month if the 'unlimited bandwidth' claim holds; unverified because the vendor page could not be read
